nd mcpjam cloud: probing, debugging, OAuth, conformance, and hosted evals from your terminal\nThe `mcpjam` CLI is two invocations.
Local MCP testing stays at the top level: inspect, debug, and test MCP servers from the command line or CI (connectivity, OAuth,
MCP Apps, tools/resources/prompts, protocol conformance). Most local commands are one-shot; `mcpjam mcp` and `subscriptions listen
` keep a process open. Account-bound commands live under `mcpjam cloud` and talk to your MCPJam account. There are no compatibilit
y aliases for the old Cloud paths; see [Migrating to CLI 4.0](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/migration.md).\nTo convert existing prom
ptfoo, pytest, Jest, or CSV tests, use the [MCP eval import skill](https://github.com/MCPJam/inspector/tree/main/skills/mcpjam-eva
l-import).\nnpx skills add mcpjam/inspector --skill mcpjam-eval-import\nTo drive MCPJam's hosted eval tools (launch a run, poll it
to a verdict, and triage a failure down to the step) use the [run MCPJam evals skill](https://github.com/MCPJam/inspector/tree/ma
in/skills/run-mcpjam-evals). This one is about running suites that already exist, not writing them.\nnpx skills add mcpjam/inspect
or --skill run-mcpjam-evals\nThese stay at the program root. They reject `--api-key` / `--api-url` / `--project`, except `test`, w
hich accepts them only to reach MCPJam-hosted inference.\n| [`test`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/local-evals) | Run an eval suite
file locally (BYOK or MCPJam-hosted inference); never uploads | `test <file>` |\n| [`oauth`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/oauth-con
formance) | Test OAuth flows and conformance against an MCP server | `conformance`, `conformance-suite`, `login`, `metadata`, `pro
xy` |\n| [`readiness`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference#readiness-hosted-commands) | Grade a server against a publisher's dir
ectory. Hosted `start` / `status` / `list` / `cancel` / `report` stay here (leaf `--api-key`; no Cloud project link) | `check`, `s
tart claude`, `start openai`, `start muse`, `status`, `list`, `cancel`, `report` |\n### MCPJam Cloud\nAccount-bound commands. Decl
are `--api-key` / `--api-url` on `mcpjam cloud` (before or after descendants). `mcpjam oauth login` is MCP-server OAuth; `mcpjam c
loud login` is your MCPJam account.\n| [`cloud`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference#cloud-workspace) | Account, project link, a
nd workspace | `login`, `logout`, `whoami`, `link`, `status`, `organizations`, `projects`, `sessions` |\n| [`cloud eval`](https://
docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference#cloud-eval-commands) | Author and run eval suites in your hosted MCPJam projects | `create`, `list`,
`run`, `status` |\n| [`cloud tunnel`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference#cloud-tunnel) | Expose a local MCP server through a p
ublic MCPJam tunnel URL, registered as a server in your project | `tunnel --server <name> <url>`, `tunnel --server <name> -- <comm
and>` |\n| [`cloud clients`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference#cloud-clients-commands) | Manage clients in your hosted MCPJam
projects (`cloud hosts` is a deprecated alias) | `list`, `get`, `create`, `update`, `servers`, `duplicate`, `delete`, `templates`
|\n| [`cloud environments`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference#cloud-environments-commands) | Manage project environments, the
host and server bundles eval suites and goals run against | `list`, `get`, `resolve`, `archive`, `ensure-adhoc` |\n| [`cloud proje
cts servers`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference#cloud-projects-servers-commands) | Connect MCP servers to a project and manage
pending connection requests | `connect`, `connect-status`, `connect-cancel` |\nAlso under `mcpjam cloud`: `goals` (`journeys` is
a deprecated alias), `personas`, `swarms`, and `studies` (which publishes an environment for outside testers and reads what they d
id; `scenarios` and `user-testing` are deprecated aliases for it). Full flag tables are in the [command reference](https://docs.mc
pjam.com/cli/reference.md).\n## Cloud credentials and API URL\n`--api-key` and `--api-url` are declared on `mcpjam cloud` and work
before or after descendants (`mcpjam cloud --api-key sk_… eval list` and `mcpjam cloud eval list --api-key sk_…` are the same). L
ocal commands, including hosted `readiness`, reject those flags at the program root. Hosted `readiness` still takes leaf `--api-ke

y`.
Credential precedence for Cloud commands:
1. `--api-key`: must be an `sk_` key. A `mcpjam_…` legacy key is a usage error.
2
. `MCPJAM_API_KEY`: same `sk_` rule. A legacy value in this env var is ignored (with a warning) so SDK eval reporting can still us
e it.\n3. Stored OAuth from `mcpjam cloud login`\n4. Missing: Cloud commands fail with login guidance before they hit the network
(`mcpjam cloud status` reports `missing` instead)\n3. The server saved with the OAuth login (only when that login is the credentia
l; a login saved before logins recorded their server counts as MCPJam Cloud, and one whose recorded server is not a usable address
is refused with exit `3`)\nEvery command that can contact MCPJam (it accepts `--api-url`, or it uploads results) decides its serv
er when it starts, before it contacts anything. An explicit `--api-url`, `MCPJAM_API_URL` or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` that is not an `htt
p(s)` URL, or that carries credentials, a query or a fragment, is a usage error (exit `2`), and so are the two variables naming di
fferent servers. The error masks credentials, a query and a fragment, and does not repeat a value that is not a URL. A saved login
is only sent to its own server: when it is the credential and the order picks another server, the command exits `3` before any re
quest. `mcpjam cloud status` uses the same checks but stays network-free: it still emits the complete JSON report, sets `ok: false
`, includes `credential.valid` / `deployment.valid` plus an `error` string, and exits `1`. Missing credentials are informational (
`credential.valid: null`) and successful.\nSuccessful Cloud commands print an audience line to stderr (`Using MCPJam Cloud as … ·
project: … · <apiUrl>`). `--quiet` suppresses it. Machine-readable JSON stays on stdout. `cloud status` redacts API keys.\n## Clou

d project scope

is file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Local Evals

> Run an MCPJam eval suite file on your mach
ine with mcpjam test with local results and an MCPJam identity\n\n`mcpjam test <file>` runs an MCPJam suite file locally: it conne
cts your MCP servers, drives each case's prompts through a model, grades the transcript with the same assertions a hosted run uses
, and decides the run with the same verdict policy. Bring your own provider key and authenticate the run with MCPJam. With MCPJam-
hosted inference it uses your existing CLI login and billing.\n\nResults are **never uploaded**. The command writes results to you
r terminal and, if you ask, to a report file. It records the run start with MCPJam. Like every command, it sends the CLI's single
anonymous [telemetry](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/telemetry.md) event, which `--no-telemetry` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` turns off; the r

un adds no telemetry of its own.

## Eval identity and local data

Run `mcpjam cloud login` locally, or set `MCPJAM_API_KEY` t
o an organization `sk_` key in CI. The SDK also accepts `apiKey` or `mcpjamAuth` in run options. Explicit credentials take precede
nce over `MCPJAM_API_KEY`, which takes precedence over the saved CLI login. An invalid explicit credential never falls back to ano
ther account. CI never starts an interactive login. Ask an organization admin for a key if you cannot create one.\n\nEvery logical
run needs an online start response. MCPJam retries transient failures within ten seconds, then stops before execution. A prior su
ccessful run does not enable offline execution. The CLI resolves the project using its existing `--project`, environment, and link
ed-project settings; a key can only access its own organization.\n\nWith results uploads disabled, the start-run request sends onl
y the credential in the authorization header, any MCPJam API headers you configure through the SDK's `inference.resolveMcpjam`, pr
oject selection, a new run-start ID, client version and surface (SDK, CLI, or Vitest), planned iteration count, provider names, an
d whether a client profile is used (`unknown` for custom executors). The server resolves the organization and account. The start-r
